derived_correctness: Every claim in Phase 3C.2's own report was independently re-derived from current source rather than trusted: (1) the highest-level entry point was confirmed by a repository-wide git grep showing auto_publish_confirmed_session has exactly one production call site (commands/phase.py::run_phase_complete); (2) the commands-zone architecture-policy correction was re-verified by directly re-running the actual AST-based dependency scanner (pcae.core.architecture.analyze_changed_python_dependencies) against every .py file in commit f4556d76, obtaining zero dependency/parse warnings, not by trusting that the pre-commit hook passed; (3) Permission Broker ALLOW/DENY/failure behavior was exercised against the real PermissionBroker/PolicyRegistry (POL-001 Missing Active Task) and a broker that raises an exception, confirming fail-closed with no unbrokered fallback; (4) no-bypass was confirmed by grep-ing the entire src/pcae tree for every call of .hand_off(/.resume_publication(, finding exactly one external production caller of hand_off (the new gate) and zero production callers of the ungated resume_publication; (5) human-authority preservation was tested for all nine non-Confirmed SessionState values via a fresh, independently-fixtured 22-test suite; (6) Repository Intelligence's deferral was re-confirmed by grepping push.py and the full diff for any RI reference (none found). This independent re-derivation surfaced one Blocking defect Phase 3C.2's own report never disclosed: auto_publish_confirmed_session's except clauses cover only the ApplicationServiceError hierarchy, but the session-lookup scan it runs first (find_session_by_subject_ref, a full scan of every persisted session) can raise SessionStoreCorruptError or PersistenceUnavailableError -- members of a separate, sibling hierarchy (InteractiveWorkflowError) -- for any corrupted/unreadable session file anywhere in the store, even one unrelated to the subject_ref being looked up. run_phase_complete wraps the call in no try/except at all, so this crashes pcae phase complete itself for unrelated phases. Reproduced twice: a standalone REPL repro and a dedicated, passing regression test (test_corrupted_unrelated_session_file_crashes_auto_publish). A second, narrower NON-BLOCKING finding was also independently reproduced: find_session_by_subject_ref resolves duplicate-subject_ref sessions by latest-created_at rather than failing closed -- a disclosed limitation in the module's own docstring, independently confirmed to have a real (if narrow) consequence. Fast Green regression correctness was independently re-derived via a genuine three-way comparison: a disposable git worktree at phase-entry HEAD (9139a2bb) reproduced 3C.2's own documented baseline exactly (338 failed, 8689 passed, 9 errors); the current tree (tests/docs/task-lifecycle files only, zero src/pcae changes) produced 339 failed/8688 passed/9 errors, reproduced identically twice; a nodeid-level diff isolated the single delta to one expected transient node (HEAD-equals-origin-main, resolved by this phase's own push) plus a pre-existing-category order-dependent swap within test_shell_gate.py::TestAuditPersistence (net zero, unrelated to this phase's diff); deselecting the union (349 nodeids) produced a fully clean run (0 failed, 8687 passed, 0 errors).
